chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, who said:
I and Ibn Faḍḍāl were sitting when Yūnus approached and said: “I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him, ‘May I be your ransom, the people have spoken much about the pillar.’”

He said: “So he said to me, ‘O Yūnus, what do you think it is? Do you regard it as a pillar of iron raised for your companion?’” He said: “I said, ‘I do not know.’” He said: “‘Rather, it is an angel entrusted with every city; Allah raises the deeds of that city by means of him.’”
He said: “Then Ibn Faḍḍāl stood, kissed his head, and said, ‘May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Muḥammad. You never cease bringing the true hadith through which Allah relieves us.’”

key_terms.الْحَدِيثِ الْحَقِّ: the true hadith that clarifies reality
key_terms.عَمُودًا: a pillar, here negated as a literal iron structure
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel appointed for a specific function

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say about the ‘pillar’ and the raising of people’s deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام clarifying that what people referred to as the ‘pillar’ was not a physical iron column, but an angel appointed over each city through whom Allah raises the deeds of its people. The report highlights unseen divine administration and the role of the Imams عليهم السلام in correcting mistaken conceptions with true hadith.
